text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Friday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian government exempts firms from interest on overdue tax payment.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic says a lot had been achieved towards normalisation of relations with Austria following his visit to that country.
- Yugoslav government adopts platform for talks of Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic with his Croatian counterpart Mate Granic in Zagreb on October 29.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Pavle Bulatovic to visit Budapest at the end of October.
- Visiting Turkish parliamentary delegation received by Serbian Parliament Speaker Dragan Tomic and Yugoslav trade minister Djordje Siradovic. A period of improved bilateral relations expected.
- There will be no visa requirement for Yugoslav citizens in eastern Slavonia as long as the UNTAES is there, says Serb justice official of the area.
- Bank of England will continue regular contacts with the National Bank of Yugoslavia, central bank vice-governor Bozidar Gazivoda said.
- Import duties for taxi cars will be reduced and they will be considered to be fixed assets, decides Yugoslav government.
- National bank of Yugoslavia will not cover insolvent banks.

- Our econonomic policy will be directed towards maintaining stability of the dinar, says Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Jovan Zebic at a pre-election gathering of the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS).
- Our strategy is offensive development and full opening towards the world, Serbian Prime Minister Mirko Marjanovic tells students.
- Serbian lawyers and private businessmen will organise a protest rally in Belgrade on October 30 over high taxes.
NASA BORBA
- The regime is demonising radicals, says Serbian Radical Party (SRS) president Vojislav Seselj.
- Serbian transport ministry has taken measures to improve financing of the country's road network, says Serbian transport minister Svetolik Kostadinovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Yugoslav commercial banks will have to adjust their business to the law on enterprises by mid 1997, it was said at a seminar organised by the Association of Yugoslav banks.
